title: Hope Bancorp Declares Quarterly Cash Dividend of $0.14 Per Share
content:
LOS ANGELES, April 28, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Hope Bancorp, Inc. (the "Company") (NASDAQ: HOPE) today announced that its Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.14 per common share. The dividend is payable on or about May 22, 2026, to all stockholders of record as of the close of business on May 8, 2026.

About Hope Bancorp, Inc.

Hope Bancorp, Inc. (NASDAQ: HOPE) is the holding company for Bank of Hope, with $18.66 billion in total assets as of March 31, 2026. Following the addition of Territorial Savings as a division of Bank of Hope, the Company became the largest regional bank serving multicultural customers across the continental United States and Hawaii. Headquartered in Los Angeles, Bank of Hope offers a comprehensive range of commercial, corporate, and consumer banking products and services, including commercial and commercial real estate lending, SBA lending, residential mortgage and consumer lending, treasury management, foreign exchange solutions, interest rate derivatives, and international trade finance. Bank of Hope operates 45 full-service branches in California, New York, New Jersey, Washington, Texas, Illinois, Alabama and Georgia under the Bank of Hope banner, and 28 branches in Hawaii under the Territorial Savings banner. Bank of Hope also operates SBA loan production offices, commercial loan production offices, and residential mortgage loan production offices throughout the United States, and a representative office in Seoul, South Korea. Bank of Hope is a California-chartered bank, and its deposits are insured by the FDIC to the extent provided by law. Bank of Hope is an Equal Opportunity Lender. For additional information, please go to www.bankofhope.com for Bank of Hope and www.tsbhawaii.bank for Territorial Savings, a division of Bank of Hope. By including the foregoing website address links, the Company does not intend to and shall not be deemed to incorporate by reference any material contained or accessible therein.

title: Bancorp Q1 Earnings Call Highlights
content:
Bancorp logo

Key Points

Management reported strong fintech-driven results with $1.41 EPS (18% YoY), a 35.1% return on equity, and fintech gross dollar volume and revenue growth accelerating (GDV +18% YoY; revenue +15% YoY). Loan growth was led by credit sponsorship—ending loans of $7.75 billion (+22% YoY) with sponsorship activity accounting for ~88% of linked-quarter loan growth and rising to ~21% of total loans, with management targeting 30–40% of the balance sheet over the next 3–4 years. Management reiterated financial targets and capital plans, guiding to $5.90 EPS for 2026 and $8.10–$8.30 for 2027, and forecasting $200 million of buybacks in 2026 (≈$50M/quarter) with 2027 buybacks expected to be near 100% of net income. Interested in The Bancorp, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Should The Bancorp Make Your Small-Cap Watchlist for 2023?

Bancorp (NASDAQ:TBBK) management used its first-quarter 2026 earnings call to highlight continued growth in its fintech-focused businesses, rapid expansion in credit sponsorship lending, and reiterated full-year earnings and capital return targets, while also providing updates on asset quality and an owned real estate property.

Quarterly performance and fintech growth

Chief Executive Officer Damian Kozlowski said the company earned $1.41 per share and posted 18% year-over-year EPS growth. He added that first-quarter return on equity was 35.1% and return on assets was 2.57%.

→ Pipelines and Automation: 2 Energy Plays Built for Any Oil Price

Kozlowski said “fintech GDV continues to grow above trend at 18% year-over-year,” and that revenue growth for the quarter—combining fee and spread revenue—was 15% year-over-year. He also said the company’s “three main fintech initiatives continue to move forward quickly and are well-positioned for success,” supported by onboarding new programs and expanding existing ones.

Credit sponsorship lending drives loan growth

Chief Financial Officer Dominic Canuso said ending loans were $7.75 billion, reflecting 9% non-annualized linked-quarter growth and 22% growth year-over-year. Canuso emphasized that credit sponsorship was the primary driver, accounting for 88% of total linked-quarter loan growth and 83% of total year-over-year loan growth.

→ Homebuilder Earnings: D.R. Horton Sticks Out as Pulte & NVR Sales Tank

Canuso said credit sponsorship balances grew to roughly 21% of total loans, up from 15% in the prior quarter and 9% a year earlier. Kozlowski separately noted that “credit sponsorship balances soared in the first quarter to $1.65 billion.”

Management described the mix shift as strategic. Canuso said the company plans to continue moving the portfolio “towards the higher returning, lower cost credit sponsorship business.” Kozlowski told analysts that the share of the balance sheet dedicated to sponsorship loans could rise over time, stating the company originally envisioned about 10% and later “more like 30% or 40% of the balance sheet possibly in the next three to four years,” while noting the Chime relationship is “a very special case” and “very unlikely to happen” at the same scale with many other partners.

Story Continues

Deposits, margin trends, and fee contributions

→ Meta Platforms Earnings Preview: What to Watch in Q1 2026 Report

Canuso said average deposits grew 9% non-annualized linked-quarter, fully funding loan growth, and average deposit cost was 1.7%, down 7 basis points from the prior quarter and 53 basis points lower than the year-ago quarter. He also cited $1.34 billion in off-balance-sheet deposits at quarter-end, up from $850 million at the end of the fourth quarter and $793 million a year earlier, which he said demonstrated continued growth in the partnership-based deposit franchise and liquidity.

Net interest margin (NIM) was 3.87%, down 43 basis points from the prior quarter and 20 basis points from the year-ago quarter. Canuso attributed the sequential decline to the loan mix shift toward credit sponsorship and “the lagged impact of the lower short-term rates on variable rate loans.”

He also provided additional context on how fintech-related fees intersect with margin:

Fintech lending fees were “the equivalent to an additional 24 basis points of net interest margin,” according to Canuso. The company generated $900,000 from deposit sweep fees tied to off-balance-sheet deposits, recorded in other income, which Canuso said equated to another 4 basis points of net interest margin.

During Q&A, Canuso confirmed that deposit sweep fee revenue tied to off-balance-sheet deposits is reported in other income. He also said the first quarter is “seasonally high just because of tax season,” and described the sweep fee contribution as a “secondary or tertiary benefit” relative to other strategies.

On the revenue mix, Canuso said net interest income mix (excluding credit enhancement) was 33%, up from 30% in the fourth quarter and 29% in the year-ago quarter, while fintech fee revenue represented 29%, compared with 27% in both the prior quarter and year-ago quarter. He said the strong growth in credit sponsorship loans is a “leading indicator” of fintech fee growth, both for lending fees and transaction fees due to higher churn.

Program launches and embedded finance timeline

Kozlowski said the company has launched its Cash App program, which “will ramp up during 2026 and 2027 and show progressive accretion” to results. In response to a question about whether the launch contributed to the quarter’s acceleration in GDV, he said there was “very little” contribution in the first quarter due to testing and gating, but he expects it to become “fairly meaningful” by year-end, with additional ramp through early 2027.

Management also reiterated expectations for additional program launches. Kozlowski said the company expects to launch “at least two significant additional programs in 2026,” though announcements depend on partners’ marketing timelines.

On embedded finance, Kozlowski told Raymond James analyst Joe Yanchunis that there is “very little revenue in store for embedded finance in 2026” and that the impact would be felt in 2027 and 2028. He said the company is “close to completing the development of its first operational use case” and plans to announce at least one embedded finance client in 2026.

Credit quality improvements, The Aubrey update, and guidance

Management reported progress on criticized assets. Kozlowski said criticized assets (substandard and special mention) declined from $194.5 million to $163.1 million, or 16% quarter-over-quarter, and he said he expects further progress over the next few quarters.

Canuso highlighted improvement in certain portfolios, “with particular note in REBL and leasing.” He said REBL criticized loans fell $24 million, or 29%, to $59 million from the prior quarter and were down 75% over the last 18 months. Excluding fintech credit sponsorship loans that are supported by “full credit enhancement,” Canuso said the traditional lending portfolio recorded a $1.3 million provision reversal, which he attributed primarily to specific reserve reductions in the leasing portfolio tied to improving borrower performance.

During Q&A, Canuso said about a third of the REBL portfolio is variable rate, contributing to lower yields as short-term rates fell. He also said recapitalizations and refinancings occurred at lower rates because properties were at more stabilized values and involved stronger investors, adding that management expects “much more stability going forward” after working through what he described as a large vintage “bubble.”

On The Aubrey property, Canuso said the company continues to invest to increase occupancy and finish upgrades. He said occupancy of available rooms has been 80% even as capacity doubled, and the company is “just over 60% of occupancy on a total unit basis,” with expectations to reach “near 70% in the very near term.” Canuso said the property is expected to be operating break even by the end of the current quarter, making its impact “neutral.” Kozlowski said the company’s intention is to finish reconditioning remaining buildings, increase occupancy to a stabilized level in the high 80s to low 90s, and then monetize the asset, though he cautioned timing depends on stabilization and potential buyer interest.

Kozlowski reiterated guidance of $5.90 EPS for 2026, including $1.75 in the fourth quarter, and said expected 2027 EPS is $8.10 to $8.30. He also reiterated capital return plans, stating 2026 buybacks are forecast at $200 million total (or $50 million per quarter), with 2027 buybacks expected to be “near 100% of net income.” Kozlowski said the company’s fintech initiatives, efficiency gains (including restructuring and AI tools), and continued buybacks are expected to be key drivers of EPS accretion, while noting results depend on development and implementation timelines in fintech.

About Bancorp (NASDAQ:TBBK)

The Bancorp, Inc (NASDAQ: TBBK) is a Delaware-chartered bank holding company that provides a range of banking and financial services to individuals, businesses, and financial institutions across the United States. Through its subsidiary, The Bancorp Bank, the company offers FDIC-insured deposit accounts, cash management solutions and specialized lending products. Its business model focuses on partnering with fintech firms, asset managers and payment processors to deliver integrated banking-as-a-service (BaaS) capabilities.

The company's product suite includes interest-bearing and non-interest-bearing checking accounts, money market accounts, certificates of deposit and debit and credit card services.

title: TBBK Q1 Deep Dive: Fintech Lending Growth Drives Strategic Shift Amid Revenue Decline
content:
Financial services company The Bancorp (NASDAQ:TBBK) fell short of the market’s revenue expectations in Q1 CY2026, with sales falling 23.8% year on year to $133.7 million. Its non-GAAP profit of $1.41 per share was 5.5% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

Is now the time to buy TBBK? Find out in our full research report (it’s free).

The Bancorp (TBBK) Q1 CY2026 Highlights:

Revenue: $133.7 million vs analyst estimates of $195.3 million (23.8% year-on-year decline, 31.5% miss) Adjusted EPS: $1.41 vs analyst estimates of $1.34 (5.5% beat) Market Capitalization: $2.53 billion

StockStory’s Take

The Bancorp’s first quarter results for 2026 were met with a negative market response, driven by a sharp year-on-year revenue decline that missed Wall Street expectations. Management attributed the performance to a deliberate shift toward credit sponsorship lending and ongoing investments in core fintech initiatives. CEO Damian Kozlowski acknowledged the headwinds in net interest margin as the company transitioned its loan mix, while noting that fintech lending fees and deposit strategies partly offset the lower spread income. Kozlowski also emphasized continued progress in reducing criticized assets and highlighted efficiency improvements through cost controls and technology investments.

Looking ahead, management’s forward guidance is shaped by expectations for continued expansion in fintech lending programs, the launch of new embedded finance offerings, and further growth in off-balance sheet deposits. Kozlowski cautioned that while embedded finance will see minimal revenue contribution in 2026, it is expected to ramp in subsequent years. The company is prioritizing operational efficiency through artificial intelligence tools and restructuring, with CFO Dominic Canuso stating, “We are leveraging AI and refilling costs across the organization to continue to improve efficiency and allocate resources to support our fintech initiatives.”

Key Insights from Management’s Remarks

Management cited rapid growth in credit sponsorship lending, fintech fee expansion, and progress on new product launches as the main contributors to the quarter’s operating results.

Credit Sponsorship Expansion: The company rapidly increased its credit sponsorship loan balances, which now account for a significantly larger share of the total loan book. Management described this as a foundational pillar for future fintech-driven revenue and noted that these loans offer lower origination costs and no risk of loss due to credit enhancements. Fintech Fee Revenue Growth: Fee income from fintech-related activities continued to rise, making up a larger percentage of total non-interest income. This reflects higher transaction volumes and deeper relationships with key partners, especially in the areas of secured lending and banking-as-a-service programs. Deposit Franchise Strength: The Bancorp emphasized growth in average deposits and a reduction in funding costs, enabled by effective deposit management strategies. Off-balance sheet deposits also grew, providing additional liquidity and secondary revenue streams, though management said these are “gravy” compared to core fintech initiatives. New Product Launches and Partnerships: The quarter saw the launch of new cash-at-program products, with ramp-up expected through the year. Management is also progressing toward additional significant program launches and an operational embedded finance platform, with at least one client announcement anticipated in 2026. Asset Quality Improvements: Criticized assets, including substandard and special mention loans, declined meaningfully over the quarter. Management highlighted ongoing improvements in the REBL (real estate bridge lending) book and leasing portfolios, with a focus on stabilizing valuations before potential asset monetization.

Story Continues

Drivers of Future Performance

The Bancorp’s outlook is anchored by continued growth in fintech lending, new program launches, and efficiency gains, while acknowledging execution risks tied to partner timelines and product mix.

Fintech Lending and Program Ramp-Up: The company expects fintech credit sponsorship and banking-as-a-service programs to drive most of its loan and fee growth. Management indicated new partner onboarding and program launches will be key to reaching targeted loan balances and revenue milestones. Embedded Finance and Technology Investments: While embedded finance revenue will be limited in 2026, management expects this segment to become a material contributor as development completes and client relationships are formalized. Ongoing investments in AI and platform restructuring are intended to improve efficiency and support scalable growth. Deposit Strategies and Asset Monetization: The Bancorp plans to further optimize its deposit mix, moving higher-cost deposits off-balance sheet and capturing incremental fee income. The timing and economics of monetizing assets like the Aubrey property, as well as ongoing share buybacks, will also impact capital allocation and shareholder returns.

Catalysts in Upcoming Quarters

Looking ahead, the StockStory team will be tracking (1) the pace of new fintech program launches and onboarding of embedded finance clients, (2) ongoing improvements in asset quality and the stabilization or sale of properties like Aubrey, and (3) the execution of deposit optimization strategies, including off-balance sheet deposit growth. Continued progress in AI-driven efficiency and capital return policies will also be important signposts.

Revenue Growth: 15% year-over-year for the quarter, including both fee and spread revenue. Release Date: April 24, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript.

Positive Points

The Bancorp Inc (NASDAQ:TBBK) reported an 18% year-over-year growth in EPS, reaching $1.41 per share. First quarter ROE was impressive at 35.1%, with ROA at 2.57%. Revenue growth for the quarter was 15% year-over-year, driven by both fee and spread revenue. Credit sponsorship balances increased significantly by 50% over the previous quarter, reaching $1.65 billion. The company is maintaining its guidance for 2026 EPS at $5.90, with expectations for 2027 EPS in the range of $8.10 to $8.30.

Negative Points

Net interest margin (NIM) decreased by 43 basis points from the prior quarter, driven by a mix shift in loans and lower short-term rates. The embedded finance platform is expected to have minimal revenue impact in 2026, with more significant contributions anticipated in 2027 and 2028. The company is facing challenges in the real estate market, with plans to stabilize and eventually sell the Aubrey property, which may take longer than initially expected. There is a potential risk associated with the proposed executive order on banks requiring citizenship information, which could impact operations. The fintech loan growth, while strong, may not immediately translate into higher net interest margins due to the unique structure and economics of these loans.

Story Continues

Q & A Highlights

Q: Can you elaborate on the embedded finance offering and its impact on 2026 results? How long will it take to onboard the first partner after announcement? A: We expect minimal revenue from embedded finance in 2026, with more significant contributions in 2027. Announcing a partner will take time, as building out capabilities can vary in scope. The impact will be more pronounced in 2027 and 2028, with more immediate revenue expected from sponsored lending growth and potential new partner announcements.

Q: How should we expect the off-balance sheet deposit strategy to evolve over the coming quarters? A: The strategy involves taking higher-cost deposits off the balance sheet, which may provide some spread, though it's not a major part of our forecast. The focus is on growing other initiatives, with off-balance sheet deposits being a secondary benefit.

Q: What are your current thoughts on the timing of selling the Aubrey property, and how will the proceeds be used? A: We plan to stabilize the property by increasing occupancy and completing upgrades, aiming for breakeven operation by the end of the quarter. The sale is expected in the first quarter of next year, with proceeds likely contributing to share buybacks, maintaining our strategy of returning 100% of net income to shareholders.

Q: How much of your balance sheet are you willing to dedicate to credit-sponsored loans over time? A: We are open to dedicating a significant portion of our balance sheet to credit-sponsored loans, potentially reaching 30% to 40% over the next three to four years. This will depend on the programs and the unique nature of partnerships like Chime.

Q: Could you discuss the shift in loan loss reserves for fintech loans and the pace of fintech loan growth? A: The shift in reserves is due to a mix shift towards secured products, which require lower reserves. Fintech loan growth has been strong, with a target of $2 billion by year-end. This growth is expected to positively impact fee income and NIM, with the balance sheet reflecting higher volumes earlier than anticipated.

Switzer, KBW: Pressed on fintech loan economics and velocity/holding periods; CEO Kozlowski said loans may be held “from 3 to 30 days…Usually, it's only a few days,” and added, “We intend to securitize a lot of it.”

 	*
Switzer, KBW: Asked about proposed citizenship-information executive order; CEO Kozlowski: “we can't really comment on it,” while noting “we do collect a lot of…information like social security numbers…for many of our” accounts depending on type.

SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

 	*
Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to neutral, focusing on timing risk and economics, including “partner delays are a thing in this space” (Joseph Yanchunis, Raymond James) and detailed pressure-testing of fintech lending yields and NIM (Timothy Switzer, KBW).

 	*
Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more explanatory in Q&A, repeatedly emphasizing timing and uncertainty, including “very little revenue…in '26” for embedded finance (CEO Kozlowski) and describing off-balance-sheet deposit economics as “gravy” and “volatile” (CEO Kozlowski).

 	*
Versus the prior quarter, the Q&A stayed centered on fintech ramp timing, but moved deeper into balance sheet allocation, loan velocity/securitization mechanics, and potential regulatory operational burden.

QUARTER-OVER-QUARTER COMPARISON

 	*
Kozlowski maintained the 2026 EPS guidance at $5.90, while shifting 2027 framing from “$8.25 a share” previously to “a range $8.10 to $8.30” now.

 	*
Credit sponsorship balances accelerated from “$1.1 billion” at Q4 2025 to “$1.65 billion” in Q1 2026, with Kozlowski calling the increase “a 50% nonannualized increase over the fourth quarter of '25.”

 	*
Off-balance sheet deposits expanded from “$400 million” (Q4 2025 discussion) to “$1.34 billion” (Q1 2026), with Canuso pointing to “continued growth of our partnership-based deposit franchise.”

 	*
NIM expectations previously contemplated compression “near 4%” (CFO Canuso in Q4), while Q1 reported NIM at 3.87% and management spent more time explaining fee-equivalent margin components.

RISKS AND CONCERNS

 	*
Management repeatedly flagged fintech execution timing risk, with Kozlowski saying announcements are “subject to our partners' marketing time lines” and embedded finance “does take a while to fully build out the capability.”

 	*
Canuso highlighted NIM sensitivity to mix and rate dynamics: “The decrease versus prior quarter is driven by both the mix shift in loans to credit sponsorship and the lagged impact of the lower short-term rates on variable rate loans.”

 	*
The Aubrey remains an operational focus and potential timing variable; Canuso said it is expected to be “operating breakeven by the end of this quarter,” while Kozlowski described a multi-phase reconditioning plan.

FINAL TAKEAWAY

Management reiterated $5.90 EPS guidance for 2026 and a $1.75 Q4 2026 EPS target while describing fintech-driven balance sheet repositioning toward credit sponsorship loans, larger off-balance sheet deposit flows, and continued buybacks (forecast at $200M in 2026). In Q&A, executives repeatedly emphasized that embedded finance contributes “very little revenue” in 2026, with the main financial ramp tied to credit sponsorship growth, Cash App scaling through 2026 and into 2027, and continued execution on partner-dependent timelines.

title: The Bancorp, Inc. Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
The Bancorp, Inc. Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance and Operational Drivers

Performance was driven by 18% year-over-year growth in Fintech Gross Dollar Volume (GDV) and a 15% increase in total revenue across fee and spread channels. Credit sponsorship balances grew 50% non-annualized in Q1 to $1.65 billion, now representing 21% of total loans as management shifts the mix toward higher-returning, lower-cost assets. The onboarding of the Cash App program has launched and is expected to show progressive financial accretion throughout 2026 and 2027. Operational efficiency is being enhanced through organizational restructuring and the deployment of AI tools to reallocate resources toward fintech initiatives. Management attributed the 16% quarter-over-quarter decline in criticized assets to successful resolution of substandard and special mention loans, particularly in the real estate bridge lending (REBL) portfolio. The bank is utilizing off-balance sheet deposits to manage liquidity and funding costs, effectively moving higher-cost deposits off the balance sheet while maintaining a robust liquidity position.

Strategic Outlook and Guidance Assumptions

Management reiterated 2026 EPS guidance of $5.90 and provided a 2027 EPS target range of $8.10 to $8.30, predicated on the ramp-up of major fintech initiatives. The 2026 capital allocation strategy includes $200 million in total share buybacks, with 2027 buybacks projected to equal nearly 100% of net income. At least two significant additional credit sponsorship programs and one embedded finance client are planned for announcement in 2026, subject to partner marketing timelines. The embedded finance platform is expected to have minimal revenue impact in 2026, with the primary financial contribution occurring in 2027 and 2028 as use cases are fully built out. Management expects the Aubrey property to reach operating breakeven by the end of Q1 2026, with a potential monetization event following stabilization at the end of 2027.

Risk Factors and Structural Dynamics

Net Interest Margin (NIM) decreased 43 basis points sequentially to 3.87%, driven by the mix shift toward credit sponsorship and the lagged impact of lower short-term rates on variable loans. A $1.3 million provision reversal in the traditional lending portfolio was primarily driven by specific reserve reductions in the leasing portfolio as borrower conditions improved. The REBL portfolio's maturity profile has improved as a large 'vintage bubble' of loans from the prior origination period has worked through the system. Management noted that while the Chime relationship currently yields a blended NIM of approximately 3%, it carries no risk of loss and significantly lower operational costs than traditional lending.

Profitability and economics of the fintech credit sponsorship portfolio

Management explained that while these loans yield approximately 3% NIM, they are 'almost like a bond' because they are credit-enhanced with no risk of loss and require a fraction of traditional lending's cost structure. The relationship with Chime is described as unique and synergistic, where lending is just one of multiple revenue streams including interchange fees and deposit funding.

Timeline and strategy for the Aubrey property monetization

The bank has shifted from a quick exit to a stabilization strategy, aiming to finish upgrading the remaining 50 units to reach 80-90% occupancy. Monetization is likely a 2027 event once the property reaches stabilized valuation, which management believes will result in better economics for the bank.

Future balance sheet allocation to credit-sponsored loans

Management indicated a willingness to dedicate 30% to 40% of the balance sheet to credit-sponsored loans over the next 3 to 4 years. Future programs may involve higher velocity and securitization, where loans are held for only 3 to 30 days before being purchased back by partners.
